newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 10.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning.

News Corp Ltd filed a lawsuit Wednesday seeking to block the proposed merger of Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting Systems Inc, contending those companies and Ted Turner were intent on stifling competition from its Fox News Channel. In the lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, News Corp asks for US$1 billion in punitive damages for alleged violations of antitrust laws and to compensate for damages it said Fox News suffered when Time Warner reneged on a promise to carry the new 24-hour channel on its cable television network.
* The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.12 (-0.23)

Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said Wednesday it reached an agreement on sharing of economic benefits with one of the four native groups near the site of its proposed diamond mine in Canada's Northwest Territories. Jim Excell, the BHP manager of the Lac de Gras mine project, said an accord had been concluded with the so-called Treaty 11 Dogrib people subject to ratification by the group's members.

Argyle Diamonds, 60 percent owned by RTZ Corp PLc-CRA Ltd and 40 percent owned by Ashton Mining, said on Wednesday it saw strong growth in India's diamond and diamond jewellery exports continuing, particularly in the U.S. market. Argyle managing director Gordon Gilchrist told a news conference in Bombay, details of which were published in London, that Argyle, Ashton and RTZ/CRA intended to be long term players in the diamond industry.

Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Wednesday it was confused by Bankers Trust Australia's comments on Wednesday that its bid for transport group TNT Ltd was at the lower end of valuations. The chairman of TNT Ltd, Fred Millar, said he did not expect the A$2.0 billion takeover bid by telecoms and postal firm Koninklijke PTT to be matched. "Until I read the press this morning it (the chance of a rival bid for TNT) hadn't even entered my mind," Millar told Reuters. "I wouldn't think so, but I don't know," he said.

Ratings agency Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it had assigned its B2 rating to Australis Media Ltd's new offering of US$150 million of senior secured discount notes due 2002. Moody's also said it confirmed the Caa rating on Australis' previously issued US$175 million of senior subordinated notes due 2003.
